subject: Learning Methods
title: Competence and Flow
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Competence and Flow.

hook.text: A chess player loses track of time for three hours. She is in flow: perfectly matched challenge meets perfect skill.

buildup.text: Csikszentmihalyi discovered flow state in the 1970s. It occurs when challenge slightly exceeds current skill level.

discovery.text: Flow requires competence feedback. You need to see progress and feel growing mastery. Without feedback, flow breaks.

twist.text: Too easy causes boredom. Too hard causes anxiety. The narrow band between them is where motivation and learning peak.

climax.text: Adjust challenge to stay in the flow zone. If bored, raise difficulty. If anxious, build more foundational skills first.

punchline.text: Challenge just beyond skill. That is where flow lives.

quiz.question: What condition triggers flow state?
options: Challenge slightly exceeds current skill with clear feedback
Working in a completely silent environment
